title: Tree nursery workdays and community plantings
summary: Volunteers help grow trees and shrubs at the nursery and plant trees in San Jose neighborhoods. Dated events are listed on the organization's Eventbrite page.
schedule: Nursery Thu-Fri 9am-12pm, Sat 9am-2pm; plantings most Saturdays in planting season
min_age_note: Age not stated; signed waiver required

title: Community habitat restoration workdays
summary: Volunteers weed, mulch, plant native species (Nov-Feb), collect seed and remove litter at preserves and creek sites. Prior registration is required for every event.
schedule: See page (workdays listed on calendar)
min_age_note: Page says all ages welcome; Youth Stewards program is for middle and high school students

title: Open space preserve stewardship projects
summary: Volunteers join single-day restoration and trail projects, or train as docents and longer-term trail stewards. Group projects typically take 8-15 people.
schedule: See page

title: Shoreline wetland restoration programs
summary: Volunteers plant native species, transplant seedlings and remove invasive plants at bay shoreline sites. Site directions are sent one to two weeks before each event.
schedule: Programs run 3-4 hours; dates on calendar
min_age_note: Children welcome with a parent or guardian

title: Bird surveys, marsh restoration and outreach tabling
summary: Volunteers staff outreach tables year-round, join tidal marsh restoration workdays, and sign up for seasonal bird monitoring surveys. Most survey programs open at set times of year and bird banding is waitlisted.
schedule: Tabling year-round; surveys seasonal; see page
min_age_note: 16+ for tabling and some monitoring; several surveys are 18+

title: Park habitat and historic landscape projects
summary: Volunteers work on habitat restoration, historic garden maintenance and beach projects in the Golden Gate national parks. Individual project sessions are listed with their own registration links.
schedule: Recurring weekday and weekend sessions; see page

title: Adopt-A-Creek litter cleanup program
summary: Groups adopt a section of a Santa Clara County creek and remove litter and graffiti. Application is by PDF form sent to the program, not an online signup.
schedule: Group sets its own dates; at least two cleanups per year
min_age_note: Children may take part with adult supervision

title: Creek trash cleanups (TEAM 222)
summary: Volunteers spend about two hours collecting trash along San Jose creeks. Event dates and registration are on the group's Eventbrite page.
schedule: Second Saturday, every other month, 2 hours; other dates on Eventbrite

title: Monthly beach and creek cleanups
summary: Volunteers pick up litter at assigned beaches and creeks led by site captains. Each site has a fixed weekend of the month and a registration and waiver form.
schedule: Weekends 9am-11am; each beach has a fixed week of the month

title: Rose garden, orchard and trail workdays
summary: Volunteers maintain the Heritage Rose Garden and historic orchard and join trail cleanups in Guadalupe River Park. Workdays need advance registration by email.
schedule: Rose garden Sat 8:30-11:30am; orchard typically Wed 9:30-11:30am; trail cleanup third Saturday
min_age_note: Most activities 10+; groups with anyone under 16 need chaperones

title: Farm Team and garden volunteering
summary: Drop-in volunteers weed and tend crops on the farm, and others care for gardens, trails or farm animals. Education guide and ambassador roles need an application and a regular commitment.
schedule: Farm Team Wed and Sat 9am-12pm; other roles vary
min_age_note: Farm Team 12+ with an adult; Garden Keeper 9+ with an adult; ambassador 16+; guides 18+

title: Fruit harvesting for food agencies
summary: Volunteers pick and sort fruit at backyard and orchard harvests in the South Bay and Peninsula. Harvest dates are on the events calendar and volunteers register through a form.
schedule: See page (events calendar)
min_age_note: Page says most ages; parent consent form for minors

title: Warehouse food sorting shifts
summary: Volunteers sort and box food, check quality and unload produce in the warehouse, lifting up to 25 lbs. Other individual roles include helping at community food distributions.
schedule: Cypress Center: weekday mornings from 9am (3 hrs), Wed 6-8pm, Sat 9am-12pm
min_age_note: 12-15 must volunteer with an adult; under 18 need a permission slip 48 hours ahead; Curtner Center is adults only

title: Home grocery delivery to seniors
summary: Volunteers use their own vehicle to load and deliver grocery boxes to homebound seniors and people with disabilities along a set route. A California driver's license, insurance and a background check are required.
schedule: See page

title: Warehouse and pantry volunteering
summary: Volunteers accept and sort donations, bag produce and help customers in the warehouse. New volunteers apply through the organization's volunteer portal.
schedule: Monday-Saturday, flexible shifts
min_age_note: Page describes 7th-8th graders taking part with an adult chaperone; confirm youth rules with the org

title: Kitchen, meal service and grocery packing
summary: Volunteers help in the kitchen, serve meals from food trucks, deliver meals to homebound adults, pack groceries and work in the community garden. Shifts are booked through the volunteer portal after signing an agreement.
schedule: See page (shifts in volunteer portal)
min_age_note: 14 is stated for families; individual minimum not stated

title: Meal prep and meal service shifts
summary: Volunteers chop produce, make sandwiches, assemble packaged meals and serve food. Every volunteer must register for a shift in advance; walk-ins are not accepted.
schedule: Shifts of 1.5-3 hours; dates on signup platform
min_age_note: Ages 12-13 may volunteer with an adult present

title: Food market, front desk and donation pickup
summary: Volunteers sort food and serve clients in the food market, check in clients, pick up grocery donations and drive older adults to appointments. Seasonal programs include back-to-school and holiday distributions.
schedule: See page
min_age_note: Page says all ages

title: Grocery packing and drive-through distribution
summary: Volunteers sort, pack and load groceries in the warehouse or work outdoor stations at the drive-through distribution, lifting 25-30 lbs. Student and monthly family volunteer options are offered separately.
schedule: Distributions 1st-4th Wednesday each month; students Mon-Fri 9am-4pm; Family Night 2nd Thursday 6-8pm
min_age_note: Student volunteers are high schoolers 14+ with parent signature; Family Nights are for ages 4-12 with a parent

title: Warehouse shifts and grocery delivery
summary: Volunteers repack dry goods, sort produce and pack food boxes in the warehouse, or drive grocery deliveries to about 15 households per route. Signing up requires creating an account on the food bank's volunteer site.
schedule: Shifts posted quarterly; delivery routes about 3 hours, Mon-Sat in SF
min_age_note: Pennsylvania Ave warehouse: 10 on weekdays, 8 on Saturdays; other warehouses 11; delivery drivers 18+

title: Sorting materials and assembling STEAM kits
summary: Volunteers sort donated materials, assemble and package classroom activity kits and help in the educator workroom. Company teams can book kit-build days.
schedule: Tuesday-Sunday, morning and afternoon shifts

title: Reading tutors, homework help and adult literacy
summary: Volunteers tutor K-4 readers, help students with homework, or tutor adults in literacy and English. Teen roles include leadership activities and writing book reviews for service hours.
schedule: See page

title: One-on-one reading tutor
summary: Volunteers tutor one elementary student in reading each week using a provided lesson plan, in person at a partner school or online. Training is provided and no experience is needed.
schedule: About 1 hour per week; Mon-Thu between 8am and 5pm
min_age_note: 14+ in person; 18+ online

title: Science and nature education volunteers
summary: Adult volunteers are trained to teach hands-on science and nature lessons to students in classrooms and the community. Separate teen docent, college and corporate group options are listed.
schedule: See page

title: Shelter volunteers and Helpful Hands shifts
summary: Helpful Hands volunteers do shelter laundry and dishes and can sign up now. Animal care, adoption and pet pantry roles recruit from a waitlist and ask for a six-month commitment.
schedule: Helpful Hands: flexible 2-hour shifts, 10-hour minimum; other roles weekly or bi-weekly for 6 months
min_age_note: Under 18 can help from home (crafts, fostering with an adult)

title: Animal shelter volunteer positions
summary: Volunteers support staff across shelter departments caring for animals and assisting the public. A volunteer pack costing $35-$42 is required after acceptance.
schedule: 2-4 hours per week for one year; juniors 2 hours for 6 months
min_age_note: 13-15 with a parent or guardian; 16-17 limited roles alone; 18+ for general roles

title: Zoo docent, keeper aide and gardener roles
summary: Volunteers host exhibits and animal meet-and-greets, assist keepers with cleaning and diets, or maintain gardens. The page says the 2026 season is full and 2027 applications are open, submitted as a PDF.
schedule: Docent 4 hours/month; Keeper Aide one day/week 9am-1pm for 6 months
min_age_note: ZooTeen program is for ages 14-17

title: Wellness calls, home visits and group projects for seniors
summary: Individual volunteers make weekly wellness calls or home visits to older adults, or train as Medicare counselors. Groups assemble gift bags, write cards, teach digital skills or do home beautification.
schedule: Varies by role; e.g. wellness calls 1+ hour/week for 2+ months
min_age_note: Page says all ages; home visits and internships 18+; digital literacy high school age and up

title: Gallery, greeter and special event volunteers
summary: Adult volunteers staff galleries, greet visitors and support special events at the science center. Corporate groups of 8-12 can book half-day or full-day activities.
schedule: Two shifts per month for 6 months; orientation offered monthly
min_age_note: Separate teen program; age not stated

title: Docent, tour guide, gardener and trolley roles
summary: Volunteers host exhibitions, lead tours, garden, assist at events or operate the historic trolley at History Park. One application form covers all roles.
schedule: Docents usually Sat-Sun 12-4pm, 1+ shift/month for a year; gardeners Mon-Fri flexible

title: Event, program and grounds volunteers
summary: Volunteers greet school groups, help run events and fundraisers, and lead hikes. Group teams do trail cleanup, grounds repair and painting.
schedule: Year-round; many evenings and weekends
min_age_note: Youth volunteer forms are linked; no age floor stated

title: Collections and archives volunteers
summary: Volunteers catalog and organize artifacts and archival material at offsite facilities; prior collections experience is required. The page marks docent, demonstrator and visitor roles as not currently recruiting.
schedule: One-year commitment; shift times not stated
min_age_note: Background check required

title: Civic tech hack nights
summary: Volunteers work on local civic technology projects such as community mapping and a tool for counting handouts. Technical skills are not required and new members are onboarded at each meeting.
schedule: Typically fourth Thursday of the month, 6:30pm

title: Court Appointed Special Advocate (CASA)
summary: Volunteers advocate for a child in foster care, visiting several times a month and attending court hearings. The role needs 30 hours of pre-service training.
schedule: About 10-13 hours per month; up to 18 months per case

title: Volunteer crisis counselor (text-based)
summary: Volunteers respond by text to people in crisis from their own computer. The role needs about 15 hours of online training and a background check.
schedule: 200 hours of conversations after training; self-scheduled

title: Online tutor for middle and high school students
summary: Volunteers tutor low-income students one-on-one online, mostly by text chat on homework questions. Volunteers complete training and certify in at least one subject.
schedule: No minimum commitment or shifts; sessions average 30 minutes
min_age_note: High school volunteers must be in 9th grade or higher

title: Citizen Archivist transcription and tagging
summary: Volunteers transcribe historical documents and tag photographs and records in the National Archives Catalog online. Contributors register for a catalog account to start.
schedule: Ongoing; self-paced

title: Remote humanitarian mapping
summary: Volunteers trace buildings and roads from satellite imagery into OpenStreetMap for humanitarian use. Groups can organize their own mapathons.
schedule: Ongoing; self-paced, plus scheduled events
